prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

TEXT_C:
Labour’s 2024 manifesto sets out a fiscally responsible plan to “stop the chaos,” restore stability and rebuild Britain around five national missions, underpinned by strong foundations in national security, secure borders and economic stability. Fiscal rules require the current budget to balance and debt to fall as a share of GDP by year five. Labour pledges no rises in National Insurance, basic/higher/additional Income Tax rates or VAT; it will fund plans by abolishing non-dom status, closing avoidance loopholes (including carried interest and offshore trusts) and modernising HMRC.

Five missions
1) Kickstart economic growth: A pro-business, pro-worker industrial strategy with an independent Industrial Strategy Council; a £7.3bn National Wealth Fund to crowd in private investment; planning reform and 1.5m homes; deeper devolution with Local Growth Plans; a New Deal for Working People (ban exploitative zero-hours and fire-and-rehire; day-one rights; stronger enforcement; minimum wage based on living costs and without age bands). Cap corporation tax at 25% for the Parliament; retain full expensing; replace business rates; 10-year infrastructure strategy and a National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority; rail brought into public ownership as contracts expire; bus franchising/municipal ownership; EV charging rollout and restore 2030 ICE phase-out; fix 1m potholes annually; nationwide gigabit and 5G by 2030; a Regulatory Innovation Office and binding rules for frontier AI; support SMEs (late payments, procurement, British Business Bank reform). Reduce net migration by linking visas to skills plans and tougher enforcement; merge Jobcentre Plus and the National Careers Service; a youth guarantee for 18–21s.

2) Make Britain a clean energy superpower: Zero-carbon electricity by 2030 via doubling onshore wind, tripling solar, quadrupling offshore wind; invest in CCS, hydrogen and long-duration storage; back nuclear (extend existing, deliver Hinkley/Sizewell C, support SMRs); maintain a strategic gas reserve; no new oil and gas exploration licences (manage existing fields). Create Great British Energy (£8.3bn) to co-invest and scale local power; Warm Homes Plan (£6.6bn) to upgrade 5m homes; British Jobs Bonus to anchor supply chains; green finance leadership and a carbon border mechanism. Restore nature and clean up rivers with tougher water regulation; support British farmers; strengthen animal welfare.

3) Take back our streets: A Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee (thousands more officers/PCSOs); new Respect Orders; specific offence for assaults on shopworkers and tougher shoplifting rules; halve knife crime with mandatory interventions and bans on machetes/zombie knives and online sales; Young Futures hubs; specialist rape units and fast-track courts; higher policing standards and vetting; a fraud strategy; expand prison capacity and cut reoffending; Hillsborough Law and action on historical injustices.

4) Break down barriers to opportunity: 3,000 school-based nurseries; 6,500 new teachers; free breakfast clubs in every primary; curriculum and assessment review; SEND inclusion; mental health support in every school; Skills England; Technical Excellence Colleges; reform the Apprenticeship Levy to a flexible Growth and Skills Levy; improve HE access and funding; broaden access to arts/sport and a football regulator; a Race Equality Act, disability/ethnicity pay-gap reporting, a full ban on conversion practices, and modernised gender recognition law.

5) Build an NHS fit for the future: 40,000 extra weekly appointments (evenings/weekends) and shared waiting lists; use independent sector capacity; double CT/MRI scanners; deliver the New Hospitals Programme; upgrade the NHS app; safer maternity care; more GPs, continuity of care and modern booking; expand pharmacist prescribing and direct referrals; Neighbourhood Health Centres; a Dentistry Rescue Plan (700,000 urgent appointments, contract reform, supervised toothbrushing); a National Care Service with national standards and a Fair Pay Agreement; 8,500 extra mental health staff and Young Futures hubs; robust public health measures (smoking/vaping, junk-food ads, energy drinks, online/gambling harms); tackle health inequalities, prioritise women’s health and aim to end new HIV cases by 2030.

Serving the country and foreign policy: An independent Ethics and Integrity Commission; modernise Commons rules and ban MPs’ paid consultancy; Lords reform (end hereditary peers, retirement at 80) and consult on replacement; votes at 16; reset relations with devolved governments; uphold the ECHR. Unshakeable NATO and nuclear deterrent; Strategic Defence Review on a path to 2.5% of GDP; defence industrial strategy; steadfast support for Ukraine (including using frozen Russian assets); AUKUS; pragmatic China policy. Make Brexit work with a better EU relationship (no single market/customs union/FoM), sector deals (e.g., veterinary, MRAs), and a security pact. Targeted trade deals aligned to the industrial strategy; lead a Clean Power Alliance; rebuild international development capacity and restore 0.7% when fiscal space allows.

First steps for change
- Economic stability with tough spending rules
- Cut NHS waits with 40,000 extra weekly appointments
- New Border Security Command
- Create Great British Energy
- Crack down on antisocial behaviour
- Recruit 6,500 teachers in key subjects

TEXT_E:
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2024 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core promise: A Fair Deal built on five themes — a stronger green economy, reliable public services, a cleaner environment, a fairer democracy, and a more outward-looking UK.

Economy and jobs
- Drive growth via a green industrial strategy, major investment in renewables, home insulation and skills.
- Fix EU relations, cut trade barriers, rejoin key programmes (Horizon, Erasmus) and aim long term to rejoin the Single Market.
- Support small business: abolish business rates and replace with a Commercial Landowner Levy; tackle late payments; expand British Business Bank; local banking.
- Fair taxes: reverse big bank tax cuts; proper windfall tax on oil/gas; raise Digital Services Tax to 6%; close CGT loopholes; 4% levy on FTSE-100 share buybacks.
- Workforce: replace apprenticeship levy with flexible skills levy; Lifelong Skills Grants (£5,000, aiming for £10,000); modernise gig-economy rights; fix sick pay; expand parental leave and pay.

Climate and energy
- Net zero by 2045; 90% of electricity from renewables by 2030.
- Ten-year emergency home upgrade: free insulation/heat pumps for low-income households; zero‑carbon standard for all new homes.
- Rooftop solar push; social energy tariff; decouple electricity prices from gas; ban fracking and new coal; scale storage and interconnectors.
- Empower community energy; climate leadership abroad; end fossil fuel subsidies.

Health and care
- Legal right to see a GP within 7 days (24 hours urgent), recruit 8,000 more GPs; universal 24/7 booking; expand Pharmacy First.
- NHS dentistry: urgent and emergency access guaranteed; fix contracts; supervised toothbrushing; scrap VAT on kids’ toothpaste/brushes.
- Mental health: walk‑in hubs for young people; school mental health professionals; regular check‑ups; end out‑of‑area placements.
- Cancer: 100% treatment within 62 days; more radiotherapy machines; more cancer nurses; faster access to new treatments.
- Social care: free personal care; Carer’s Minimum Wage (+£2/hour); Royal College of Care Workers; paid carer’s leave and respite; cross‑party funding deal.

Education and families
- Per‑pupil funding to rise above inflation; fix crumbling buildings; Tutoring Guarantee for disadvantaged pupils.
- Early years: extra five free hours for disadvantaged 3–4s; triple Early Years Pupil Premium.
- Restore maintenance grants; Lifelong Skills Grants; teacher workforce plan; SEND funding reform; arts protected.
- Parental support: double statutory maternity/shared parental pay to £350/week; extra use‑it‑or‑lose‑it month for fathers at 90% pay; day‑one rights incl. self‑employed.
- Extend free school meals to all children in poverty.

Housing
- Build 380,000 homes a year, including 150,000 social; 10 new garden cities; use‑it‑or‑lose‑it permissions; Rent to Own model.
- Renters’ rights: ban no‑fault evictions; default three‑year tenancies; landlord register.
- Abolish leasehold; cap ground rents; remove dangerous cladding at no cost to leaseholders.
- End rough sleeping; scrap Vagrancy Act.

Nature and water
- End sewage scandal: transform water firms into public benefit companies; ban bonuses until discharges end; tougher regulator; Sewage Tax; real-time spill data.
- Double nature by 2050; 60m trees/year; Clean Air Act and new Air Quality Agency; stronger watchdogs (OEP, EA, Natural England).

Crime and justice
- Restore community policing; guarantee police attendance and investigation of all burglaries.
- Cut court backlogs; Online Crime Agency; scrap Police and Crime Commissioners; end disproportionate Stop & Search; youth diversion nationwide.

Transport
- Accelerate EV switch: mass charging rollout, restore plug‑in grant, 2030 ZEV sales rule; cut VAT on public charging.
- Freeze rail fares; simplify ticketing; electrify rail; Northern Powerhouse Rail; empower councils to franchise buses; nationwide active travel plan; fix potholes.
- Reform aviation taxes; super-tax private jets; ban short flights where rail <2.5 hours (unless low/zero‑emission).

Immigration and asylum
- End Hostile Environment; scrap Illegal Migration Act and Rwanda plan; 3‑month target to process most asylum claims; allow work after 3 months; expand safe/legal routes.
- Merit‑based work visas; reverse family threshold hike; protect EU citizens; expand Youth Mobility.

Rights, democracy, defence, international
- Protect Human Rights Act; ban conversion therapy; scrap anti‑protest laws; flexible working right; right to work from home for disabled people.
- Proportional representation (STV) for MPs and English councils; votes at 16; cap donations; federal UK with written constitution.
- Defence: reverse Army cuts; target 2.5% of GDP; maintain nuclear deterrent; tighter arms export controls.
- Foreign policy: rebuild EU ties; support Ukraine (use seized Russian assets); restore aid to 0.7%; immediate ceasefire and two‑state solution, recognise Palestine; stand up to China/Russia; fund BBC World Service.

Judge whether A or B aligns more closely with this profile, taking into account that each foundation may be invoked in either direction.
